Like other New Yorkers, you’re likely utilizing the city’s public transportation on a daily basis to get around New York City. One of these options includes the subway system, which runs through the different parts of the city, from the Bronx, Manhattan, Queens, to Brooklyn. Folks who need to commute daily to work will often choose to live in a neighborhood that has an NYC subway stop that directly connects to work. During the last few months, we spent time going over the various train routes and neighborhoods along those particular subway lines and covered the R train route in our last article. Today, we’re moving on to the next yellow local W train train route. We’ll go over each of the subway stations the W train stops at and discuss the best neighborhoods to live in on its route.


# W train stops NYC


Compared to other yellow trains on the route, the W train is quite short. There are only a total of 7 stops in Queens and 16 stops in Manhattan for the W train route. This route starts off in Astoria in Queens and works its way southward until it crosses from Queens to Manhattan at the Queensboro Plaza station. In Manhattan, the W train continues westward until it reaches the 57 St-7 Av stop and then heads southward towards downtown Manhattan. Eventually, the W train reaches its terminal station at the very south tip of Manhattan at the Whitehall St-South Ferry stop.


In order from Queens and Manhattan is a list of stops that the W train stops at. We’ve specifically pointed out stops that service the local W train. For your convenience, we’ve also marked the stops that are ADA accessible.


### Queens stops:


- Astoria-Ditmars Blvd (Local) (Terminal) – also services N route


- Astoria Blvd (ADA accessible) (Local) – also services N, M60 SBS to LGA Airport


- 30 Av (Local) – also services N route


- Broadway (Local) – also services N route


- 36 Av (Local) – also services N route


- 39 Av (Local) – also services N route


- Queensboro Plaza (ADA accessible) (Local and Express) – also services N and 7 route


### Manhattan stops:


- Lexington Av/59 St (Local) – also services R, N, 4, 5, 6, F, Q route


- 5 Av/59 St (Local) – also services R, N route


- 57-7 Av (ADA accessible) (Local and Express) – also services Q, R, N route


- 49 St (ADA accessible) (Local) – also services R, N route


- Times Sq-42 St (ADA accessible) (Local and Express) – also services A, C, E, Q, R, 1, 2, 3, 7 route


- 34 St-Herald Sq (ADA accessible) (Local and Express) – also services B, D, F, M, Q, R, N route


- 28 St (Local) – also services R route


- 23 St (Local) – also services R route


- 14 St-Union Sq (ADA accessible) (Local and Express) – also services L, N, Q, R, 4, 5, 6 route


- 8 St-NYU (Local) – also services R route


- Prince St (Local) – also services R route


- Canal St (Local and Express) – also services J, Q, N, R, Z, 6 route


- City Hall (Local) – also services R route


- Cortlandt St (ADA accessible) (Local) – also services A, C, E, R, 2, 3 route


- Rector St (Local) – also services R route


- Whitehall St-South Ferry (Local) – also services R, 1 route


You can also locate a


[W train stops map in PDF format](https://www.mta.info/maps/subway-line-maps/w-line) directly on the MTA’s site. Alternatively, you can read through a


[text format of the W train stops map here](https://www.mta.info/maps/subway-line-maps/r-line) .


## Best Queens neighborhoods along W train stops


### Astoria


Located on the northwest tip of Queens is the relatively large neighborhood of


[Astoria](https://www.renthop.com/apartments-for-rent/astoria-new-york-ny) . This neighborhood is bounded by the East River to the west, Long Island City to the south west, Sunnyside to the southeast, and Woodside and East Elmhurst to the east. Over the last century, the population of Astoria has grown tremendously and today, the neighborhood’s population is estimated close to 200,000. Astoria is known for its diverse population with people from over 100 different countries represented in its population breakdown.


The neighborhood is popular with folks from all walks of life. The neighborhood is popular with folks from college students, young professionals, families, etc. It’s proximity to Manhattan makes it additionally popular with folks who want to live nearby but who want to save a bit more on their monthly rent. As a result, businesses have poured in from all over and residents of the neighborhood have access to a plethora of restaurants, cafes, bars, shops, etc.


## Best Manhattan neighborhoods along W train stops


### Herald Square


The area of Herald Square is located within the hustle and bustle of


[Midtown Manhattan](https://www.renthop.com/apartments-for-rent/midtown-manhattan-new-york-ny) . Herald Square is located close by to Penn Station is made up of mostly commercial buildings and home to major department stores and national brands such as Macy’s, Target, Primark, Sephora, H&M, etc. A haven for shoppers, the area is also home to a few known apartment complexes such as Herald Towers, Beatrice Apartments, and The Epic. These towers aren’t the most affordable, but given their locations to the middle of Manhattan, can be alluring choices for many looking for quick access to the heart of Manhattan.


Residents of the neighborhood will have access to one of the best Koreatowns in America along with plenty of other restaurants, bars, and cafes in the general Midtown area. Looking to check out other parts of Manhattan? Residents can easily hop on the various subway lines from locations across the neighborhood.


### Washington Square Park


Yet another area that isn’t exactly a neighborhood but is still popular with residents is Washington Square Park in the neighborhood of


[Greenwich Village](https://www.renthop.com/apartments-for-rent/greenwich-village-new-york-ny) . A lot of the immediate buildings surrounding this park are dorms or housing complexes that belong to New York University. However, there are a few options available, such as the Heritage Apartments just south of the park. This area is popular with folks other than students, faculty, and NYU staff and is popular for a reason. The area has plenty to offer, from cute boutiques that are a pleasure to explore and walk through, to historical streets such as MacDougal Street, that have plenty to offer in addition to their businesses and restaurants.
